Subject: SwiftPay urgent: dedicated pool saturation + reserved throughput shortfall — ops assist + exec ask

Team —

SwiftPay (priority enterprise; committed reserved throughput) reports rising 5xx and long tail latency on their reserved endpoint. Customer artifacts attached. Key customer ask: immediate mitigation to stabilize their checkout flow and an ETA for resolution.

What I’m seeing from dashboards (quick summary):
- SwiftPay’s reserved tokens show no obvious over-consumption in the console.
- Dedicated GPU pool serving model-llama-70b shows average GPU utilization at 92% with sustained queuing (token queue depth up 3x).
- Top contributors are a small cohort of long-context requests and several large-batch offline jobs that weren’t scheduled during the maintenance window.

Short-term mitigation proposals (need ops / eng approval):
1) Emergency burst authorization (spin up 8 burst nodes in the dedicated pool for 2 hours) — requires exec sign-off for quota increase.
2) Temporary routing: route SwiftPay to a compatible hosted variant (llama-70b-quantized) for high-priority routes for up to 1 hour while we heal the dedicated pool.
3) Apply conservative cross-tenant throttles to non-priority customers on the hot hosts (10% token throttle) to free headroom.
4) Quick kernel rollback to the previous runtime build if we confirm a regression tied to the recent kernel change.

Customer-facing asks I’m prepared to make (pending approval):
- Offer a 10% invoice credit for the hour of impacted traffic and guarantee a post-mortem within 48 hours.

Please respond with: (A) operational approach we can run now, (B) whether spike is due to scheduling (we can preempt those batch jobs), (C) exec/finance approval for burst and credit.

I’ve attached internal pool metrics (redwood-internal-pool-metrics-0624.csv) and the customer logs.

– Sean

Attachments: redwood-internal-pool-metrics-0624.csv

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: SwiftPay urgent: dedicated pool saturation + reserved throughput shortfall — ops assist + exec ask

Sean / team —

Quick diagnostics summary after triage:
- Root cause: a kernel selection regression in the 2026-06-23 runtime release combined with two concurrent large offline batching workloads landing on the same host shard. The kernel mismatch causes suboptimal attention compute on specific sequences (long-context) and increases per-token latency; queueing increased as a result.
- Impact: SwiftPay is top of the hot-shard consumer list, hence their reserved throughput appeared to be "short" because headroom was consumed by queueing on the host level.

Immediate actions executed (already running):
1) Isolated the two offline jobs and re-scheduled them to cold hosts (completed by 10:05 PDT).
2) Rolled runtime kernels back to 2026-06-22 on the affected shard cluster; kernel rollback completed at 10:42 PDT. Metrics show initial queue depth reduction ~35%.
3) Spun up 6 burst nodes as a stop-gap (will remain online for 3 hours).
4) Applied a 10% cross-tenant throttle to the non-reserved traffic on the affected hosts to prioritize reserved customers.

Remaining asks:
- Exec approval to keep the 6 burst nodes for an additional 4 hours if needed (billing/quotas).
- Sales / customer success confirmation about customer credit (Sean / Marissa) — recommended 10% credit for the impacted 2-hour window.

Next steps and ETA:
- Short-term: we expect queue depth and tail latency to fall to acceptable SLOs within 30–45 minutes (we already see improvement).
- Medium-term: ops will run an automated placement-tuning job to avoid hot-shard concentration (ETA 24 hours).
- Post-mortem and action items will be ready within 48 hours.

I’ll continue to monitor and will post metrics to the incident ticket.

—David
David Kim
Principal Infra Engineer — Redwood Inference
